title: Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit
shortDescription: Cooling fan 1 control circuit reports a fault.
fullDescription: DTC P0480: Cooling fan 1 control circuit reports a fault. Emissions and cooling fan controls keep the engine, A/C, and EGR system in their target ranges. A failure here usually triggers the MIL and may force engine derate to protect components.
safetyImpact: An inoperative cooling fan can lead to overheating in slow traffic. EGR faults raise emissions and may cause hesitation but are not an immediate hazard.

causes.cause: Failed cooling fan motor or relay
Stuck or carboned EGR valve / sensor

symptoms: Check engine light
Engine running hot in stop-and-go traffic
A/C performance loss
Hesitation or surge on light throttle
Audible fan running constantly or never

fixSteps.title: Scan and Verify Operation
fixSteps.instruction: Command the fan or EGR with the scan tool's bidirectional control. Confirm whether the actuator responds and live data tracks the command.

fixSteps.title: Check Power and Ground
fixSteps.instruction: Verify battery voltage and ground at the actuator connector while commanded on. Inspect related fuses and relays.

fixSteps.title: Test the Component
fixSteps.instruction: Bench-test the relay, fan motor, or EGR valve/sensor per service manual. Replace any unit that fails its spec.

fixSteps.title: Repair Wiring or Replace Component
fixSteps.instruction: Repair harness damage or replace the failed actuator. Clear codes and verify with a road test and follow-up scan.

faq.q: Can I drive with a cooling fan code?
faq.a: Short trips at speed are fine — airflow cools the radiator. Avoid traffic and idling until repaired.

faq.q: Will an EGR cleaning fix this?
faq.a: Often yes — carbon buildup is the most common cause of EGR position/flow codes. A solvent soak or replacement valve usually resolves it.

faq.q: Is this an expensive repair?
faq.a: Most fan and EGR repairs are under $400 at a shop. Wiring repairs are cheaper if you DIY but tedious to trace.
